headline: BOE Warns Scale and Breadth Of AI Financing Poses Threat to Financial Stability

paragraphs.text: The artificial-intelligence investment boom is supporting global economic growth, but the scale and breadth of financing that it requires is making the global financial system more vulnerable to setbacks, the Bank of England said Thursday.

In its twice-yearly report on the health of the financial system, the BOE estimated that AI-related bond issuance by large technology firms known as hyperscalers will more than double to exceed $305 billion this year, or around 8% of total bond issuance by investment-grade corporations.

Adding bond issuance by semiconductor manufacturers and data-center operators would leave the "broader ecosystem" borrowing more than the governments of some large advanced economies, including the U.K., the BOE said.

"The growth and broadening of markets used to finance AI-related investment is deepening interconnections across the system, making it more likely for stress in one area to propagate to another," the BOE said.

The U.K.'s central bank expects the financing needs of AI-related businesses to increase further in 2027, and reach into more segments of the system to include investment-grade bonds, leveraged finance and private credit, and public and private equity.

The BOE said the scale of the financing that is driving the AI investment boom might be so large that it is "contributing to upward pressure on global real interest rates," making it more expensive for governments, households and other businesses to borrow.

An additional source of risk is the "opacity" of financing arrangements between businesses involved in the AI buildout, often carried out through special purpose vehicles supported by leases, purchase agreements, backstops and guarantees provided by the hyperscalers.
"Off-balance-sheet arrangements make assessing the serviceability of potential future liabilities more challenging," the BOE said.
The BOE estimates that the total debts and off-balance-sheet commitments of hyperscalers now exceed $4 trillion.
"The scale and nature of these financing commitments could come under strain in a stress or if expectations around future AI revenues were revised down," the BOE said.

Equity prices for AI-related businesses have swung wildly over recent weeks, led by chip maker Nvidia. Last week alone, the Nasdaq composite's members lost more than $4 trillion in market value, but prices have partly rebounded.
The BOE said recent market moves have been amplified by some hedge funds reducing their borrowing, but had not had a significant impact on broader financial markets.

"While spillovers to other markets were limited, in a more severe shock, losses on equity positions could also lead globally active investors to deleverage in other markets, including sovereign debt markets," the BOE said.
The central bank repeated its warnings about the threat posed by frontier AI models to the cybersecurity of financial firms and market infrastructure.

"The rapid development of open-weight AI models that could run more cheaply than proprietary models, with safeguards more easily disabled or removed, can make advanced AI models more readily available and useful to malicious actors," the BOE said.
